claims.title: Portuguese chart the 'Lion Mountains'
claims.summary: Portuguese mariners, an expedition associated with Pedro de Sintra reaching the area about 1462, charted the great harbour and named the surrounding hills Serra Lyoa, the 'Lion Mountains' — the origin of the country's name.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1462-portuguese-chart-the-lion-mountains, claim TL:SLE:event:1462:portuguese-chart-the-lion-mountains, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Rice Coast chiefdoms
claims.summary: The Sherbro, Bullom, Temne, and other peoples farmed rice, fished, and traded along the coast and rivers, organised in chiefdoms and ritual societies rather than a single state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1500-the-rice-coast-chiefdoms, claim TL:SLE:event:1500:the-rice-coast-chiefdoms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Mane incursions
claims.summary: Mande-speaking Mane raiders pushed to the coast and by the 1550s had subdued the Temne and other peoples, imposing a new ruling elite in a contested episode that reshaped the region's politics.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1550-the-mane-incursions, claim TL:SLE:event:1550:the-mane-incursions, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Emergence of the Mende
claims.summary: Out of the mingling of Mane aristocrats with indigenous Bullom and other populations the Mende identity and language took shape, spreading as a lingua franca and becoming one of Sierra Leone's largest ethnic groups.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1580-emergence-of-the-mende, claim TL:SLE:event:1580:emergence-of-the-mende, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The coast enters the Atlantic trade
claims.summary: European ships drew the rivers of the Sierra Leone coast into the transatlantic slave trade, exchanging goods and firearms for captives seized in raids and wars across the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1562-the-coast-enters-the-atlantic-trade, claim TL:SLE:event:1562:the-coast-enters-the-atlantic-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bunce Island slave fort established
claims.summary: The Royal African Company built a fortified post on Bunce Island in the Sierra Leone River, beginning the island's long and notorious role in the British slave trade.

sources.label: Bunce Island in Sierra Leone (Gilder Lehrman Center)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1670-bunce-island-slave-fort-established, claim TL:SLE:event:1670:bunce-island-slave-fort-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bunce Island at its height
claims.summary: Under the London firm of Grant, Sargent and Oswald, Bunce Island became one of the largest British slave castles on the Rice Coast, with many captives — valued as skilled rice-growers — sold to planters in South Carolina and Georgia.

sources.label: Bunce Island in Sierra Leone (Gilder Lehrman Center)
Bloody Bunce: A Legacy of the Transatlantic Slave Trade in Sierra Leone

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1750-bunce-island-at-its-height, claim TL:SLE:event:1750:bunce-island-at-its-height, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Britain abolishes the slave trade
claims.summary: The British Parliament outlawed the transatlantic slave trade, ending Bunce Island's slave-trading operations and clearing the way for Freetown to become a base for naval suppression of the traffic.

sources.label: Bloody Bunce: A Legacy of the Transatlantic Slave Trade in Sierra Leone

claims.title: The 'Province of Freedom' founded
claims.summary: Abolitionists associated with Granville Sharp settled about 400 of London's 'Black Poor' on the Sierra Leone peninsula, founding the 'Province of Freedom' and the settlement of Granville Town.

sources.label: On the Foundings of Sierra Leone, 1787–1808

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1787-the-province-of-freedom-founded, claim TL:SLE:event:1787:the-province-of-freedom-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Sierra Leone Company chartered
claims.summary: After Granville Town's destruction, the abolitionist-backed Sierra Leone Company was chartered to revive and govern the colony as a base for legitimate commerce and Christian settlement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1791-the-sierra-leone-company-chartered, claim TL:SLE:event:1791:the-sierra-leone-company-chartered, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nova Scotian settlers found Freetown
claims.summary: Some 1,100–1,200 Black settlers from Nova Scotia — African Americans who had sought freedom with the British in the American Revolution — landed and founded Freetown beneath the Lion Mountains.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1792-nova-scotian-settlers-found-freetown, claim TL:SLE:event:1792:nova-scotian-settlers-found-freetown, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jamaican Maroons arrive
claims.summary: About 550 Jamaican Maroons, exiled after the Second Maroon War, arrived in Freetown and helped put down a revolt by the Nova Scotian settlers against the Sierra Leone Company.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1800-jamaican-maroons-arrive, claim TL:SLE:event:1800:jamaican-maroons-arrive, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sierra Leone becomes a Crown Colony
claims.summary: The British Crown took over from the Sierra Leone Company, making Freetown a Crown Colony and the principal base for the Royal Navy's suppression of the Atlantic slave trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1808-sierra-leone-becomes-a-crown-colony, claim TL:SLE:event:1808:sierra-leone-becomes-a-crown-colony, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The West Africa Squadron frees the recaptives
claims.summary: Courts at Freetown emancipated more than 80,000 'Liberated Africans' rescued from slave ships by the Royal Navy's West Africa Squadron, who were resettled in and around the colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1808-the-west-africa-squadron-frees-the-recaptives, claim TL:SLE:event:1808:the-west-africa-squadron-frees-the-recaptives, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fourah Bay College founded
claims.summary: The Church Missionary Society founded Fourah Bay College in Freetown, the first Western-style university in sub-Saharan Africa, helping earn the city the name 'the Athens of West Africa'.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1827-fourah-bay-college-founded, claim TL:SLE:event:1827:fourah-bay-college-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Krio community takes shape
claims.summary: The Liberated Africans and earlier settlers fused into the Krio (Creole) people, with their English-based Krio language, Christianity, and Western education spreading influence across West Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1840-the-krio-community-takes-shape, claim TL:SLE:event:1840:the-krio-community-takes-shape, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Protectorate proclaimed
claims.summary: Britain declared a Protectorate over the interior of Sierra Leone, extending colonial rule over the Temne, Mende, and other peoples beyond the coastal Crown Colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1896-the-protectorate-proclaimed, claim TL:SLE:event:1896:the-protectorate-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Hut Tax War
claims.summary: The imposition of a tax on dwellings sparked armed resistance led by the Temne chief Bai Bureh in the north and spreading to the Mende in the south; Britain suppressed the revolt and exiled Bai Bureh.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1898-the-hut-tax-war, claim TL:SLE:event:1898:the-hut-tax-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Sierra Leone People's Party
claims.summary: Constitutional reform and the founding of the Sierra Leone People's Party under Milton Margai broadened African political participation and set the colony on the road to self-government.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1951-rise-of-the-sierra-leone-people-s-party, claim TL:SLE:event:1951:rise-of-the-sierra-leone-people-s-party, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from the United Kingdom
claims.summary: Sierra Leone became an independent state within the Commonwealth under Prime Minister Sir Milton Margai, ending British colonial rule begun in 1808.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Sierra Leone
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1961-independence-from-the-united-kingdom, claim TL:SLE:event:1961:independence-from-the-united-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sierra Leone becomes a republic
claims.summary: Sierra Leone adopted a republican constitution; two days later Prime Minister Siaka Stevens became the nation's first president, beginning a long consolidation of personal power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1971-sierra-leone-becomes-a-republic, claim TL:SLE:event:1971:sierra-leone-becomes-a-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: One-party state under the APC
claims.summary: Siaka Stevens's new constitution made Sierra Leone a one-party state under the All People's Congress, entrenching personal rule, patronage, and economic decline.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1978-one-party-state-under-the-apc, claim TL:SLE:event:1978:one-party-state-under-the-apc, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Civil war begins
claims.summary: The Revolutionary United Front under Foday Sankoh, backed by Liberia's Charles Taylor, invaded from Liberia, beginning an eleven-year civil war marked by atrocities and funded by 'blood diamonds'.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-1991-civil-war-begins, claim TL:SLE:event:1991:civil-war-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British intervention and UNAMSIL
claims.summary: As the RUF again advanced on Freetown, Britain's Operation Palliser and a strengthened UN Mission (UNAMSIL) turned the war; Foday Sankoh was captured, breaking the rebellion's momentum.

sources.label: British military intervention in the Sierra Leone Civil War (Operation Palliser)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-2000-british-intervention-and-unamsil, claim TL:SLE:event:2000:british-intervention-and-unamsil, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The civil war ends
claims.summary: With disarmament completed, the eleven-year civil war was declared over; estimates put the death toll above 120,000, with millions displaced and thousands maimed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sierra Leone: From the Mende, Temne, and Sherbro of the Rice Coast through Bunce Island and the Atlantic slave trade to Freetown's 'Province of Freedom', the Krio, the Hut Tax War, independence, and a brutal civil war survived.", terralore.co/country/SLE/chronicle#ev-2002-the-civil-war-ends, claim TL:SLE:event:2002:the-civil-war-ends, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Charles Taylor convicted
claims.summary: The UN-backed Special Court for Sierra Leone convicted former Liberian president Charles Taylor of aiding and abetting war crimes and sentenced him to 50 years — the first head of state convicted by an international tribunal since Nuremberg.

sources.label: The Prosecutor vs. Charles Ghankay Taylor
sources.publisher: Residual Special Court for Sierra Leone

sources.label: Prosecutor welcomes UN-backed court's decision to uphold Charles Taylor conviction

claims.title: The Ebola epidemic
claims.summary: An Ebola outbreak reached Sierra Leone in May 2014, killing nearly 4,000 people and overwhelming health services before the WHO declared the outbreak over in November 2015, with recovery following.

sources.label: Statement on the end of the Ebola outbreak in Sierra Leone
sources.publisher: World Health Organization, Regional Office for Africa

sources.label: Ebola virus epidemic in Sierra Leone
